thread:
Maya: Quick sync — ran into a weird gap where Private runtimes return no streaming chunks for long responses. Our client-side canary assumes chunked events and marks the run as failed. Need to decide whether to change the probe or the runtime handshake.
Asif: Ugh. Is this because the Private adapter doesn't advertise streaming capability?
Maya: Yeah — we only expose stream_capabilities in the adapter manifest, but the probe path (probe v2) defaults to expecting chunks unless the controlplane says otherwise.
Toni: Could we add a lightweight 'signal' in the probe handshake that says: expects_streaming: true|false and max_chunk_bytes? That'd be simple to check before starting.
Sam: +1. Also worth noting the Dedicated path currently supports streams but does chunking differently (smaller chunk size), so we need a compatible contract.
Asif: Agree. Proposal: make the probe handshake include a small capability object. If runtime doesn't include it, probe treats as "no-stream" fallback. That avoids breaking clients.
Maya: Draft shape I had in mind:
```
handshake: {
  runtime_id: "r-123",
  capabilities: { streaming: true, max_chunk_size: 65536, polling_fallback: "poll_v1" }
}
```
Asif: That looks fine. Two questions: 1) Should capabilities be opt-in (explicit) or opt-out? 2) How do we version it?
Toni: Make it opt-in. Old runtimes without the field mean "no streaming". For versioning, include a handshake_version int. Start at 1.
Maya: Good. Also need to update router policy: currently we route by latency/cost only. If a request requires streaming (e.g., client asked for streaming=true), we must prefer runtimes that advertise streaming.
Sam: We already have a routing predicate framework. I'll add a predicate for capabilities.streaming == true. If not found, and request requires streaming, route to hosted/dedicated fallbacks and add header X-Fallback-Reason.
Asif: What about canary metrics? Right now we sample streams differently; we need to ensure metrics ingestion tolerates polling fallback so canaries don't explode.
Maya: For canaries, treat polling as a distinct signal. In the console we should surface degradation: "streaming->polling" so PMs know quality changed.
Toni: Implementation plan: 
- Adapter change: expose handshake_version + capabilities (Asif)
- Router change: honor capabilities in route selection + X-Fallback header (Sam)
- Client/probe: check handshake and switch to polling mode if not streaming (Maya)
- Console: small UI flag for canary quality (Toni)
Sam: I'll also add a unit test in the routing predicates. Quick pseudo test:
```py
def test_route_prefers_streaming():
  req = Request(streaming=True)
  runtimes = [R(capabilities.streaming=False), R(capabilities.streaming=True)]
  chosen = route(req, runtimes)
  assert chosen.capabilities.streaming is True
```
Asif: One more edge: quantized runtimes may advertise streaming:true but internally buffer until first token due to kernel constraints. We should allow runtimes to provide a streaming_mode enum: immediate|buffered|none.
Maya: Nice catch. Replace boolean with enum (none/immediate/buffered) and keep max_chunk_size. Backwards compat: old missing field => none.
Toni: I'll update the doc and add examples. Also add a migration note for Private runtimes (they'll need a small shim).
deploy-bot: Canary deployment to staging (router + probe) succeeded :party:
Maya: Great. Action items: Asif to open adapter PR for handshake enum + version (ETA 2d). Sam to update router predicate + tests (ETA 2d). Toni to update docs + canary dashboard copy (ETA 3d). I'll update probe harness and add an integration test (ETA 3d).
Asif: I'll also add a compatibility checker that logs when runtime advertises "buffered" so ops can triage latency impact.
Sam: Sounds good. If anyone wants, I can drop a minimal proof-of-concept today that fakes two runtimes so we can validate metrics.
Maya: Please do. That will make the canary QA faster. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
